record.problem_and_user: Online clothing shoppers who can't tell how items will fit or look, driving costly returns (page cites 30-40% return rates and about $40B yearly).
record.one_line_pitch: Voice-controlled virtual clothing try-on studio using segmentation and an open-source try-on model to show users wearing garments.
record.problem_statement: Online clothing shoppers struggle with fit and look, driving costly returns and emissions.

glance.what: Automated fuzzing tool that finds bugs and security vulnerabilities in software.
glance.why: Helps developers catch vulnerabilities before shipping, protecting software and operating systems.

record.what_it_is: A Go command-line fuzzer that mutates the bytes of an input file, runs a target program on the mutated file, and records the byte position and error output when the program crashes. A defensive testing tool for developers.
record.problem_and_user: Developers of all levels who are unaware of vulnerabilities in their programs or lack an efficient way to locate them.
record.one_line_pitch: A Go fuzzer that mutates bytes of an input file, feeds it to a target program and logs the crashing byte and error.
record.problem_statement: Developers lack an easy, efficient way to find vulnerabilities in their programs.
record.devpost_tagline: This Miraculous Bits and Bytes Fuzzer aims to improve the safety and integrity of software and operating systems by enabling developers to efficiently identify vulnerabilities in their programs.
devpost_first_sections: Many developers are unaware of the potential vulnerabilities that exist in their programs. Others struggle to find an efficient, reliable way to identify the locations of their vulnerabilities. We aim to improve the safety and integrity of software by enabling developers to efficiently test the security of their programs in order to mitigate the risk of data breaches, financial losses and reputational damage.

The Miraculous Bits and Bytes Fuzzer provides a way for software developers from all levels to safely test and identify potential vulnerabilities that exist in their programs. It works by mutating the bytes of a file and sending it to a program that takes and processes the file. If the mutated file causes unexpected crashes in the program, then our fuzzer will record what byte the program crashes at and what error it outputs in a separate file.

record.problem_and_user: Everyday users who want to quickly cut a set of devices off the network during an attack, for confidential work, or when traveling in high-risk areas.
record.one_line_pitch: One-button Android app that remotely cuts Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular and ports on all a user's devices through MQTT endpoints.
record.target_user: everyday users and travelers worried about attacks
record.problem_statement: Consumer cyber defense tools are costly and complicated, with no easy way to airgap many devices at once.
record.devpost_tagline: AerLock is system consisting of a mobile app and workstation endpoints designed to safeguard all of your devices from cybersecurity threats, using airgap technology with the press of a single button.
devpost_first_sections: Many cybersecurity programs aren't suited for the average user, with high costs, lack of consumer availability, and complicated UI. We developed AerLock as a solution that places the power to defend in the hands of the average person, allowing users to lock down their suite of connected devices from a single interference easily and efficiently.

AerLock provides a secure way to remotely airgap and restore functionality on multiple devices across different operating systems by disabling or enabling communication services like Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Cellular Data, NFC, and physical ports. Integration with a MQTT broker enables AerLock to send lock or unlock commands from an Android app to an AWS cluster, triggering a responses from all machines with an installed and connected endpoint.

We originally intended to make a HTTP/S proxy, but ran into issues with maintaining the two-way connections that HTTPS required. Additionally, HTTP/S requests were relatively few and far between, and continued use could be sustained over a single long TCP/IP stream. The solution was to use a TCP proxy instead in the form of the SOCKS5 protocol. Running the proxy server on iOS mobile devices locally due to sandboxing constraints caused many headaches and would have gone beyond the scope of the project. Traveling cross country requires meticulous planning as one miscalculation can lead to disaster. To this end we have created OffTrails, a wilderness route selection aide which seeks to maximize the safety, efficiency, and speed of cross country travel.

The program pulls topological data from the US Geological Survey and water/vegetation data from ESA's Sentinel-2 L2A satellite. The resulting route will then be displayed in the WebUI and a route GPX file can be downloaded into the user's preferred map app at their convenience.

record.what_it_is: A solo project using a pretrained Google DDPM diffusion model to denoise very noisy photos by injecting the real image midway through the reverse process, and to create variations by re-adding noise ('renoising') and denoising again, with a GUI and a small API script.

devpost_first_sections: We’ve all been there: you snap a bunch of photos to capture a moment, only to look back and feel like something’s missing. Maybe the lighting was off, the image is way too grainy, or there’s a distracting detail you wish you could erase. The photo just doesn’t feel like the moment you lived. That frustration is what inspired Lighthouse — a tool designed to reconstruct and creatively reimagine noisy or imperfect images using the power of diffusion.

Lighthouse is powered by diffusion models — deep learning systems that can generate detailed, high-quality images from nothing but noise. Normally, these models start from pure randomness and gradually subtract noise in small steps, revealing an image as they go. I thought: what if we hijack this process? devpost_first_sections: We wanted to create a seamless, gesture-based authentication system for AR headsets that can easily switch between users in shared environments. Additionally, we wanted to integrate health tracking features such as heart rate monitoring and tremor detection, specifically for early onset Parkinson's. The idea of personalizing environments after authentication and simultaneously collecting health data inspired us to combine the power of AR with IoT and machine learning.

Snap Secure uses Snap AR Spectacles to authenticate users with a gesture, such as a finger tap. Once authenticated, the physical environment is adjusted to the user’s preferences (e.g., changing the color of lights). Meanwhile, the system collects health data like heart rate and tracks tremors, which can help in early diagnosis of diseases like Parkinson's as well as general health monitoring for the user. We even built models that work across different headsets from the Snap AR Spectacle to the Apple Vision Pro, and Meta Quest 2.

glance.what: Links team decisions from conversations to GitHub pull requests, checking code against them.
glance.why: Keeps implementations matching what the team actually agreed to build.

record.what_it_is: A team workspace (whydidwechoosethis.tech) that turns planning conversations, by text or voice, into versioned architecture decision records with provenance. A GitHub bot checks pull requests against published decisions, and coding agents read them through an MCP server.
record.problem_and_user: Software teams, especially multi-repo ones, whose design reasoning is scattered and whose AI coding agents add unagreed scope.
record.one_line_pitch: Workspace where teams plan with an AI assistant by text or voice, publish architecture decision records, and have a GitHub bot check pull requests against them.
record.problem_statement: Reasoning behind architecture decisions is scattered, and AI agents or contributors can drift from or invent scope without it.
record.devpost_tagline: Bridging the gap between technical documentation, and the actual implementation. Turn team conversations into shared decisions, then use AI to check GitHub pull requests against what you agreed to do.
devpost_first_sections: This started with a problem one of us had at work: one architecture decision record (ADR) can span five microservices, and enforcing it across all of them is a nightmare. In one case, an AI agent hallucinated a single bullet point about “audit logs.” That one line cost one of us hours of work across reviewers and maintainers. A small piece of invented scope became real engineering work. A repository shows what we built, but the reasoning behind it is scattered across documents, tickets, and conversations. As AI speeds up implementation, we need a better way to preserve that reasoning and check whether the code follows it. We built whydidwechoosethis.tech to keep the why with the work.

Start a project, connect your repositories, and talk with an AI assistant through text or voice about what you want to build. The assistant helps question assumptions, clarify tradeoffs, and turn the conversation into an architecture decision record. Bring teammates into the same workspace to discuss the proposal while the assistant refines the document. When the team agrees, publish a version that captures the decision. glance.why: Surfaces urgent tenant issues so property managers act on what matters.

record.what_it_is: A memory layer for commercial property managers that ingests Gmail threads, Google Sheets, voice notes, documents and maintenance photos, extracts tenant and property intelligence with Gemini, and presents a daily ranked briefing, risk heatmap and natural-language Q&A.
record.problem_and_user: Property managers whose tenant history is scattered across emails, spreadsheets and memory, so a new manager restarts from zero after a handoff.

The real problem isn’t lack of data, it’s that critical context lives in scattered systems and individual memory. Miro changes how institutional memory is handled in commercial real estate. When a property manager leaves, critical context is often fragmented across tools and incomplete handoffs, forcing the next manager to rebuild understanding from scratch. Miro solves that gap by preserving and mirroring the past

devpost_first_sections: Every UMass student has experienced or witnessed the stress of losing a UCard. Whether it's at the dining hall, library, or gym, UCards are constantly being misplaced across campus. Currently, when someone finds a lost UCard, they often don't know how to contact the owner, and the card either ends up at a random lost-and-found location or, worse, never makes it back to its owner. We realized this pain point during a conversation at Blue Wall when one of our team members found a UCard on an empty table. After spending 15 minutes trying to find the owner through social media, we thought: Then FoundU was born.

FoundU streamlines the process of returning lost UMass UCards through a simple, automated system: When someone finds a UCard, they use the app to take a photo The Google Vision API automatically extracts the student's name from the card image The system uses Puppeteer to scrape the UMass People Finder website to locate the student's email The finder can input the location where they found the card or provide their contact information Using Nodemailer, the system automatically sends an email to the cardholder with the card's photo and retrieval details

Traditional evaporative cooling systems depend on clean freshwater and often waste it in the process. As AI infrastructure continues to grow rapidly, we wanted to rethink that tradeoff. Instead of letting AI consume more water, our goal is to use its waste heat to help generate it.

Our project, Drip, combines edge computing with custom chemistry hardware to transform AI waste heat into clean water. glance.what: Screens cancer drug candidates against protein targets, ranking top compounds with quantum circuits.
glance.why: Helps researchers find promising drug candidates faster.

record.what_it_is: Devpost presents a cancer drug-candidate screener: per-target ML models narrow about 14,000 ChEMBL compounds to 10, then a VQE quantum-chemistry step scores them. The repo README instead describes a quantum drug-safety toolkit for polypharmacy.
record.problem_and_user: Researchers choosing a cancer protein target who want better early screening, since most drugs fail trials. README version targets patients, clinicians and researchers checking drug-regimen safety.
record.one_line_pitch: Drug-discovery screener that narrows 14,000 ChEMBL compounds to 10 with ML models per cancer target, then scores them with a VQE quantum chemistry step.
record.problem_statement: Most drugs fail in clinical trials because early screening misses good candidates.
record.devpost_tagline: Pick a cancer type and protein target. Helix screens thousands of compounds and ranks the top candidates with real quantum circuits, allowing researchers to identify highly targeted candidates.
devpost_first_sections: We built Helix in three layers. The first layer pulls 14,000 real drug compounds from ChEMBL, the world's largest open drug database, and trains a machine learning model on real lab experiments for each cancer protein target. The second layer runs every compound through that model to narrow 14,000 options down to 10 candidates in seconds. The third layer runs a real quantum algorithm called VQE on each of those 10 drugs to compute how stable the molecule is at a quantum chemistry level, giving researchers an extra signal that no standard tool produces.

Getting quantum circuits to work on real drug molecules was harder than expected because quantum chemistry requires molecules to have an even number of electrons, and most drug fragments do not. We had to write custom preprocessing logic to fix each molecule before it would run without crashing. Cleaning the training data was also a big challenge since the raw database had duplicate experiments and inconsistent measurements that we had to filter out before the models could learn anything useful.

record.what_it_is: Native iPhone app where two nearby people tap phones, confirm the bump, and see specific shared interests plus AI-written conversation starters drawn only from approved profile facts. Profiles are built by speaking a short intro to a Grok voice interviewer.
record.problem_and_user: Students and event attendees standing near each other who do not know what to say to start a conversation.
record.one_line_pitch: iPhone app where two nearby people tap phones together and get specific shared-interest conversation starters from a user-approved voice-built profile.
record.target_user: students and people at events or classes
record.problem_statement: People near each other want to talk but lack context for a first conversation, and loneliness is widespread.
record.devpost_tagline: Turn the people you pass into people you know
devpost_first_sections: The people you'd get along with may already be in the room. You just don't know what to say to them yet. The research points to a consistent problem: Loneliness is common. The WHO Commission on Social Connection estimates that roughly 1 in 6 people worldwide experience loneliness, including around 1 in 5 adolescents and young adults. We misjudge strangers. Commuters expected that talking to a stranger would make their ride worse, yet those who did reported a more positive experience than those who kept to themselves. The fear is worse than the conversation. Across seven studies, people's predicted fears about talking to a stranger were generally worse than their actual experience of the conv

Bump gives two people who are already near each other just enough common ground to start talking. Make a profile by talking. Give a short spoken or typed intro. Grok asks up to three follow-up questions, read aloud, and drafts a profile card. You edit and approve every line before anyone sees it. Bump. Tap your phones together. Both people confirm it was really each other before anything is exchanged. Find your overlap. Bump shows the specific interests you share, plus complementary ones: related but different interests, or one person's goal lining up with the other's experience. glance.why: Helps untrained bystanders perform life-saving CPR quickly.

record.problem_and_user: Untrained bystanders who freeze when someone collapses; the page says only about 20% of Americans are current on CPR training.
record.one_line_pitch: [redacted]

record.devpost_tagline: Pulse uses AR on Snap Spectacles to guide users through CPR in real time with visual and auditory feedback, making life-saving action fast and accessible to everyone.
devpost_first_sections: When someone collapses from cardiac arrest, every second matters. Yet most people freeze because they are unsure how to help. Only 20% of Americans are current with CPR training, and even fewer feel confident enough to act under pressure. We created Pulse to bridge that gap. Instead of relying on memory or scrambling to find a guide, users can receive calm, step-by-step CPR instructions directly in their field of view. With augmented reality through Snap Spectacles, Pulse empowers anyone to take immediate and effective action during an emergency.

Pulse is an AR application for the Snap Spectacles that provides step-by-step CPR guidance in real time. It has two main components: real-time CPR guidance and a map displaying nearby AEDs for quick retrieval. The CPR guidance component uses Snap Spectacles’ AR capabilities to walk users through each critical step of administering CPR. It directs users on where to place their hands, provides a rhythm to follow for compressions, and measures compression, ensuring accurate and effective compressions. glance.what: Self-stabilizing smart spoon that cancels hand tremors for comfortable eating.
glance.for_whom: people with Parkinson's or essential tremor
glance.why: Lets tremor patients eat comfortably and independently with an affordable device.

record.what_it_is: Arduino-based smart spoon that uses an MPU6050 motion sensor and two servos in a two-axis arrangement to keep the bowl level against hand tremors, housed in a 3D-printed handle.
record.problem_and_user: People with Parkinson's disease or essential tremor who want to eat comfortably; commercial stabilizing spoons cost over $300.
record.one_line_pitch: Self-stabilizing smart spoon using an Arduino, MPU6050 sensor and two servos to keep the bowl level against hand tremors.
record.target_user: people with Parkinson's or hand tremors
record.problem_statement: Commercial tremor-stabilizing spoons for Parkinson's cost over $300, putting them out of reach for many.
record.devpost_tagline: We built an affordable, self-stabilizing smart spoon. By instantly counteracting hand tremors with a 2-axis sensor-motor system, we help Parkinson's and essential tremors patients dine comfortably.
devpost_first_sections: When researching solutions to Parkinson's and hand tremors, we realized that spoons with actual self-stabilizing technology were very expensive, often easily above $300. Thus, we decided to try to make one with easily accessible microcontrollers, motors and sensors to make an affordable version.

The Unspillable is a smart spoon that uses a 2-axis sensor-motor system to counteract tremors and tilts in real time. The spoon bowl always remains perfectly level no matter the angle of the handle or hand.

glance.what: Voice assistant that tracks focus, prompts breaks and summarizes your computer activity.
glance.why: Helps people stay focused and rested by reviewing their daily work.

record.what_it_is: A desktop time-tracking assistant that logs active app, window title and idle time with a native C++ agent, analyzes periodic screenshots with Gemini, and shows a dashboard. A global shortcut opens a voice or text companion that answers questions about your workday.
record.problem_and_user: Computer workers who finish long screen sessions unsure what they accomplished and find to-do lists and time-blocking inaccurate.
record.one_line_pitch: Local-first desktop work companion that logs app usage into a semantic timeline and offers a voice and text AI assistant with screen context.
record.problem_statement: Time-blocking tools do not reflect reality, leaving people unclear what they actually accomplished during screen time.
record.devpost_tagline: M.I.R.A turns your computer activity into smart, voice-powered insights; tracking focus, prompting breaks, and summarizing your day with a private, conversational AI assistant.
devpost_first_sections: Mira — Intelligent Work Companion

We noticed a pattern in our own work, endless hours in front of screens, pretending to be productive, yet unclear about what we actually accomplished. Most productivity tools rely on time-blocking or to-do lists, but they rarely reflect reality. We wanted something that could see what we’re doing, understand the context, and help us think better , not just work harder. That idea became Mira , an intelligent work companion that gives users a semantic picture of their day and contextual assistance, all while keeping data local.

glance.what: Family database and social platform that keeps stories, heirlooms and documents.
glance.why: Protects family stories and documents for future generations.

record.what_it_is: A native iOS app where a voice AI companion, Loomie, talks aloud with older relatives about their memories and an analysis backend turns the stories into a shared family archive: a corkboard family tree, cross-generation 'Sparks' and a 3D globe.
record.problem_and_user: Spread-out families whose elders' oral histories and life lessons vanish unrecorded, and younger relatives who want to hear and keep them.
record.one_line_pitch: iOS app where a voice AI companion named Loomie interviews family members to turn memories into a shared living family archive.
record.problem_statement: Families scattered by distance and generations lose shared stories and a sense of connection.
record.devpost_tagline: Introducing HeirLoom, the first family-oriented database and social platform. Through AI-powered integration, we make family connections easier and protect family heirlooms, stories, and documents!
devpost_first_sections: They say it takes a village to raise a child, but what if the village no longer exists? Introducing HeirLoom, an iOS app that turns fleeting family memories into a living archive, pairing a real-time conversational voice AI oral historian with a tactile corkboard "tree" of pinned Polaroids and connecting red twine

The people who raise us shape our values and sense of self, but modern life has scattered families across different cities, demanding careers, and generational divides. Group chats that only awaken for birthday emojis offer the illusion of closeness while irreplaceable oral histories quietly disappear. Most people know little about their lineage past their grandparents, and older generations' life lessons often vanish before anyone writes them down. We wanted to move past sterile family-tree forms and impersonal photo dumps to build a warm, welcoming space where family culture actually lives and grows.

glance.what: Live forecasts of satellite re-entries, showing what survives and where it lands.
glance.why: Shows where falling satellite debris may land, for safety awareness.

record.what_it_is: A live 3D globe forecasting when decaying satellites and rocket bodies will re-enter and which components survive. GPU Monte Carlo physics runs about 20,000 simulated futures per object and a debris model breaks each into parts; SpacetimeDB is the only backend.
record.problem_and_user: The public, who get only a re-entry date window and no info on surviving debris, while breakup analyses stay inside agencies.
record.one_line_pitch: Live 3D globe forecasting when decaying satellites re-enter and which components survive, using GPU Monte Carlo physics, with SpacetimeDB as the only backend.
record.problem_statement: The public only gets a single re-entry date and no insight into surviving debris; analyses stay inside agencies.
record.devpost_tagline: Live forecasts of which satellites are falling, what survives re-entry, and where it could land, powered by GPU Monte Carlo physics and SpacetimeDB.
devpost_first_sections: In March 2024, a piece of a discarded ISS battery pallet survived re-entry and crashed through the roof of a house in Naples, Florida. Thousands of objects are decaying out of orbit right now. Low Earth orbit holds thousands of short-lived satellites; Starlink alone de-orbits satellites almost daily, and rocket stages and old debris come down too. The public answer to "what's coming down, and where?" is usually a single date with a window of hours, and no idea what actually survives. Break-up and survivability analyses stay inside agencies. We wanted to build the tool we wished existed: a live globe that shows which objects are re-entering, which pieces survive, how heavy and how dangerous t

SKYFALL runs that analysis openly and continuously, on live public data: Track every decaying satellite and rocket body from live orbit data (CelesTrak) and space weather (NOAA SWPC). Show it all live on a 3D globe. Each object is colored by its earliest plausible re-entry, so anything that could come down within a day stands out. glance.what: Custom hardware builder that prototypes device ideas with boards and sensors.
glance.why: Turns imagined devices into working prototypes quickly.

record.what_it_is: A web app where a user describes a hardware gadget in plain English and gets a visualization, a priced parts cart, starter firmware, step-by-step illustrated assembly instructions and a demo video.
record.problem_and_user: Makers, students and hobbyists who have a device idea but struggle with parts selection, specs and build planning.
record.one_line_pitch: Turns a plain-language hardware idea into a visualization, AliExpress parts cart, starter firmware and illustrated assembly steps with a demo video.
record.target_user: hobbyists and students building hardware projects
record.problem_statement: Hardware ideas are slow to realize because specs, parts and planning are unclear and hard to visualize before building.
record.devpost_tagline: You imagine it. We build it for you.
devpost_first_sections: We were inspired by how hard it is to turn hardware ideas into reality. Creativity moves fast, but hardware doesn’t. Physical constraints, unclear specs, and planning overhead slow everything down. Often, it’s hard to even visualize a hardware idea before building it. We wanted to find a solution.

All you have to do is tell Buildo what you want to build. This could be a coffee temperature checker, a plant health soil sensor, or that one class project that just seems impossible. That’s it. From there, Buildo gives you a realistic visualization of your idea, a complete shopping cart of the parts you need with specs and prices, starter firmware code you can copy and upload, and clear step-by-step assembly instructions you can download with images and a demo video. In a nutshell, Buildo turns ideas into build-ready hardware.

glance.what: Robot that learns everyday tasks zero-shot from observation using foundation models.
glance.why: Avoids costly RL training, letting robots learn tasks by watching.

record.what_it_is: A zero-shot control pipeline for a Nao humanoid robot: spoken commands and the robot's camera go to Gemini, which breaks tasks into subtasks, locates objects with bounding boxes and segmentation, and calls low-level walking and arm functions to clean spills or sort items.
record.problem_and_user: Aimed at making household-capable humanoid robots feasible without costly reinforcement-learning policy training; no specific end user named.
record.one_line_pitch: A Nao humanoid robot uses Gemini vision, spatial reasoning and function calling to plan and carry out tasks like cleaning a spill without task-specific training.
record.problem_statement: Training robots for everyday tasks through reinforcement or imitation learning is expensive and compute-heavy.
record.devpost_tagline: Our robot solves the challenge of complex task learning without intensive RL training. Using foundation models and multimodal perception, it performs everyday tasks zero-shot from observation alone.
devpost_first_sections: As a passionate roboticist, I've witnessed firsthand the transformative revolution unfolding in our field. The industry is increasingly generating rich ecocentric datasets for Physical AI development, which traditionally feed into computationally intensive reinforcement learning policies for task execution. However, this conventional approach remains prohibitively expensive and resource-demanding. This challenge inspired us to explore more efficient alternatives that could democratize advanced robotics capabilities while maintaining the sophisticated functionality needed for real-world applications.

Our humanoid robot executes complex, multi-step everyday tasks through advanced spatial understanding and reasoning capabilities. When instructed to "clean up the table" or "sort kitchen items," it intelligently distinguishes between trash and valuable objects, properly disposing of waste while organizing items that should be preserved. The robot demonstrates contextual intelligence by selecting appropriate cleaning tools—knowing when a situation calls for a paper towel versus a brush. This practical reasoning enables it to handle varied household scenarios without specific programming for each task variation, making it truly useful for daily living assistance.

glance.what: Autonomous billing-dispute analyst for satellite ground stations, resolving conflicting records.
glance.why: Turns conflicting billing records into clear decisions faster.

record.what_it_is: Claims-settlement system for satellite ground-station operators. A fast tabular model auto-settles confident SLA credit disputes, an LLM investigates hard ones with citations, AWS Cedar policy decides what may auto-pay, and rules learned from human decisions are replayed on history before a controller promotes them.
record.problem_and_user: Finance dispute analysts and controllers at ground-station operators who settle failed-pass credit claims by hand and inconsistently.
record.one_line_pitch: Autonomous agent that settles satellite ground-station SLA credit disputes by weighing pass logs, space weather, maintenance notices and contract terms, escalating to a controller when needed.
record.target_user: ground-station operators' dispute analysts and controllers
record.problem_statement: Ground-station operators settle dropped-pass billing disputes by hand across conflicting sources, which is slow at the volume of contacts they handle.
record.devpost_tagline: An autonomous dispute and billing analyst for satellite ground stations.
devpost_first_sections: Ground stations are the toll booths of space. A satellite passes overhead for a few minutes, an antenna tracks it, the data comes down, and someone sends a bill. AWS Ground Station charges by the minute. KSAT, the world's largest commercial ground-station operator, reported NOK 2.361B (about USD $234M) in 2025 group revenue across about 2.1 million contacts on about 375 antennas . At that volume, every dropped pass, partial downlink, or "the storm ate my data" email turns into a billing dispute. Right now a person settles each one by hand. glance.what: Wearable LiDAR and vision mobility aid detecting obstacles for blind users.
glance.why: Improves independent navigation and spatial awareness for visually impaired users.

record.what_it_is: A chest-mounted wearable for blind or low-vision users: a 2D lidar gives proximity beeps, a webcam with YOLO names nearby objects, and fused distance and direction are spoken aloud through a Bluetooth speaker, with a browser dashboard for caregivers.
record.problem_and_user: People with low vision who rely on a white cane, which only senses what it touches near the ground; caregivers are a secondary user of the dashboard.
record.one_line_pitch: Chest-worn assistive device pairing a 2D lidar with YOLO object detection on a Jetson Orin Nano to beep and speak obstacle names and distances to low-vision users.
record.problem_statement: White canes sense only nearby ground-level obstacles and cannot identify objects or warn of approaching ones.
record.devpost_tagline: A.U.R.A. is an AI-powered wearable mobility aid combining LiDAR and computer vision to detect nearby obstacles, improve spatial awareness, and empower blind or visually impaired individuals.
devpost_first_sections: Inspiration Millions of people with low vision rely on a white cane, which only senses what it physically touches, about a meter ahead and at ground level. It can't say what is in the way, and it can't warn about something approaching. glance.what: Money-habits app framed as a cat-collecting game with budget and gacha features.
glance.why: Makes saving money fun, rewarding good financial habits with a game.

record.what_it_is: A gamified budgeting app with a cat theme.
record.problem_and_user: Young people who find money management overwhelming; app tries to build habits through game rewards.
record.one_line_pitch: Gamified budgeting app that builds a budget and savings plan from transactions and rewards completed goals with points for a cat-collecting gacha.
record.problem_statement: Young people find managing money overwhelming; the app makes good budgeting habits rewarding through game mechanics.
record.devpost_tagline: Paws-itively better money habits!
devpost_first_sections: Seeing how young people struggle to manage their finances effectively, it can be overwhelming and lead to poor decisions. We got inspired by cat collecting mobile games. We wanted to create a product users will develop good finance habits but also make the experience interactive and fun. By adding game elements, we incentivize the user to stick to their goals to reward them for creating smart habits but also consider saving and sticking to a budget enjoyable activities.

An application that analyzes users' expenses and transactions to create an effective budget and savings plan to help them manage their finances more efficiently. If the user completes the goals, they get points to be able to purchase cats and cat accessories through a randomized character system.
